articles.title: James Webb discovers a scorching lava planet with a “giant sunscreen”
articles.description: A scorching lava planet 280 light-years away has surprised astronomers by apparently maintaining a thick atmosphere despite conditions that should have stripped it away billions of years ago. James Webb Space Telescope observations suggest that TOI-561 b reflects about 75% of incoming starlight, possibly because of mineral clouds that act like a giant sunscreen. The planet may also be continually replenishing its atmosphere through gases released from a global ocean of molten rock.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has discovered a remarkable scorching lava planet 280 light-years away that mysteriously maintains a thick atmosphere despite extreme temperatures.

articles.title: Smithsonian scientists just recreated the first 2 billion years of the Universe
articles.description: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Called Lumina, the groundbreaking simulation recreates the universe’s first 2 billion years, showing how dark matter, gas, and radiation interacted to give rise to the earliest stars, galaxies, and black holes.
articles.summary: Smithsonian scientists have created one of the most detailed simulations of the early universe's first 2 billion years, revealing new insights into cosmic structure formation and evolution.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers have made a landmark discovery of three actively feeding supermassive black holes within a single galaxy from over 12.5 billion light-years away, challenging our understanding of early black hole formation.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of what may be the first moon ever detected outside our solar system, representing a historic breakthrough in exoplanet science.

articles.title: Artemis III SLS Core Stage Joins Boosters at Kennedy
articles.description: NASA’s Artemis III SLS (Space Launch System) core stage is integrated alongside the twin solid rocket boosters on Oct. 28 inside the Vehicle Assembly Building’s High Bay 3 at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.   Technicians lifted the 212-foot rocket stage from the facility’s High Bay 2 using a one-of-a kind lifting beam designed […]
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis III Space Launch System core stage is integrated with twin solid rocket boosters at Kennedy Space Center, marking a major milestone toward returning humans to the Moon.

articles.title: Webb Sees Turbulent Star Nursery
articles.description: In this Webb image released on Oct. 22, 2026, we see a turbulent cauldron of star formation filled with dense clumps of gas. This region is named N159 and is located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This region has a lower metallicity […]
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures a stunning image of a turbulent star nursery filled with dense clumps of material actively forming new stars.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration mission launches toward Phobos, Japan's first mission to explore the enigmatic moon of Mars.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the instrument's exceptional detection capabilities.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Solar Orbiter traces the origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks in solar wind, revealing new insights into solar physics.

articles.title: NASA's New UV Space Telescope Will Launch in 2031
articles.description: NASA has committed to launching a new, more powerful UV space telescope. Named UVEX, the UltraViolet EXplorer, it will launch in 2031. It's about 100 times more powerful than its predecessor, GALEX, whose mission ended in 2013. UVEX will perform a survey in UV that will complement infrared surveys by other telescopes.
articles.summary: NASA's upcoming UVEX (UltraViolet EXplorer) space telescope will launch in 2031, providing unprecedented ultraviolet observations to advance our understanding of the universe.

articles.title: The Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory found a distant Solar System object before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time even got started. The object is a dwarf planet candidate named 2026 ED138, and if confirmed, it will be one of the largest dwarf planets beyond Neptune. It may be up to 1500 km in diameter.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered its first dwarf planet candidate, demonstrating the observatory's capability to detect distant Solar System objects ahead of its major Legacy Survey.

articles.title: NASA Systems Engineering Team Details HWO Mission Architecture
articles.description: Finding an Earth-like world beyond the solar system is the Holy Grail of exoplanet research, and the field has experienced incredible technological advancements in searching for and identifying exoplanets since the first exoplanet was discovered in 1995. This includes both ground- and space-based telescopes, specifically the powerful James Webb Space Telescope. However, directly imaging exoplanets remains elusive, primarily due to the enormous technological challenge of imaging a point of light so far away.
articles.summary: NASA's systems engineering team has detailed the architecture for the Habitable Worlds Observatory mission, advancing the quest to discover Earth-like exoplanets.

articles.title: Sun's outer magnetic field mapped in 3D for the first time
articles.description: A team of researchers has produced the first global, three-dimensional estimates of the sun's magnetic field, including the area beyond the sun's visible edge. This marks a step toward more accurate models of solar activity—and ultimately, better predictions of solar magnetic eruptions, which are the root cause of extreme space weather that can impact critical infrastructure technologies on Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers have produced the first comprehensive 3D map of the Sun's outer magnetic field, revealing new details about solar structure and activity.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory reveals its first dwarf planet candidate in our solar system
articles.description: Scientists may add a new dwarf planet to the official roster of our solar system. The distant, icy body, provisionally dubbed 2026 ED138, orbits our system beyond Pluto. It was spotted earlier this month by a scientist combing through data from the Simonyi Survey Telescope at the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Rubin Observatory has identified a potential new dwarf planet candidate in our solar system, expanding our understanding of distant icy bodies in the outer reaches of our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: Double debris disk orbiting a dead star hints at our solar system's future
articles.description: Astronomers using the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (ESO's VLT) have found a rare disk of debris around a dead star that provides a glimpse of what may happen to our solar system. Unlike in similar systems previously found, the debris—the leftovers of planets that once orbited the star—is organized in a double disk, the two parts separated by a clear gap. The disk appears to be shaped by two planetary bodies, one possibly as big as Pluto, that have survived the violent death of the star.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Very Large Telescope has discovered a rare double debris disk around a dead star, offering insights into how planetary systems evolve and hints at the distant future of our own solar system.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis I mission reveals surprising radiation levels near the Moon
articles.description: NASA’s Artemis I mission has revealed that cosmic radiation near the Moon is higher than in Earth orbit, but not by as much as scientists might expect. Tiny experimental detectors also uncovered surprising details about how radiation passes through the human body, offering valuable insights for future lunar exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis I mission has provided crucial data on radiation levels near the Moon, advancing our understanding of the lunar environment for future human exploration.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from NASA's asteroid Bennu are revealing 4.5-billion-year-old secrets that are rewriting our understanding of how the solar system formed.

articles.title: Astronomers found a mysterious object beyond Neptune, and it could be a new dwarf planet
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered a suspected dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit. If confirmed, it would be the sixth known dwarf planet in our solar system.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered a suspected dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit, potentially adding a new member to our solar system's outer reaches.

articles.title: A small star is eating a brown dwarf so slowly that the meal could last billions of years, and the two orbit each other every 87 minutes inside a space that would fit within the Sun
articles.description: A small red star is pulling gas from a brown dwarf as the pair circles every 87 minutes, packed into an orbit that could fit inside the Sun. Material strikes the star’s surface and lights up a hot spot, marking a meal that could continue for billions of years…
articles.summary: A remarkable binary system features a red star slowly consuming a brown dwarf over billions of years while orbiting every 87 minutes in an incredibly compact space.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Scientists explore the giant-impact hypothesis, where a planet-sized object collided with Earth to form our Moon during the early solar system's formation.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory looks toward its next 90 years of innovation, envisioning interstellar probes, lunar drones, and helicopters exploring Mars.

articles.title: NASA Welcomes Vietnam as Newest Artemis Accords Signatory
articles.description: The Socialist Republic of Vietnam became the 78th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, joining a growing coalition of like-minded nations committed to the peaceful, transparent, and responsible exploration of space.   “Vietnam is joining at an important point in the development of its own space program,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson in recorded remarks […]
articles.summary: Vietnam becomes the 78th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, expanding the international coalition for sustainable lunar exploration and peaceful space cooperation.

articles.title: NASA Selects 19 New Citizen Science Proposals in 2026
articles.description: So far, 2026 has seen a flood of successes for volunteers who do NASA science, exemplifying NASA’s commitment to gold-standard science—transparent, reproducible and intrinsically collaborative. The Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 project announced that their project volunteers have now discovered most of the known brown dwarfs, celestial objects that are similar to planets. The Zooniverse platform, […]
articles.summary: NASA selects 19 new citizen science proposals for 2026, demonstrating the agency's commitment to engaging volunteers in groundbreaking scientific research.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: A spectacular image showcases stars actively forming within a nebulous cauldron of cosmic gas and dust.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo mission celebrates eight years of its groundbreaking journey to explore the planet Mercury with innovative scientific instruments.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration mission launches on an H3 rocket to explore the mysteries of Mars's moon Phobos.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: European Space Agency's Mars Express has revealed new insights into Martian atmospheric phenomena, discovering that Mars's unusual clouds may be even more complex than previously understood.

articles.title: Betelgeuse Is Disturbed By Its Companion Star
articles.description: Betelgeuse has a close-orbiting companion that disturbs the red supergiant into an egg-like shape. New observations show how the two stars interact and how this could help explain the varying brightness of Betelgeuse.
articles.summary: New observations reveal that Betelgeuse's companion star gravitationally distorts the red supergiant into an egg-like shape, offering fresh insights into binary star systems.

articles.title: Glowing Salt Crystals Tracked Radiation Aboard Artemis I
articles.description: There weren’t any humans strapped into the bucket seats of the Orion spacecraft for the Artemis I mission. But there were two anthropomorphic mannequins made to mimic human bone and soft tissue, but also equipped with hundreds of radiation sensors spread throughout their body as part of the Matroshka AstroRad Radiation Experiment. A recent paper led by Paweł Bilski of the Institute for Nuclear Physics of the Polish Academy of Sciences, and published in the journal Radiation Measurements, reports on the results of that experiment, including the operation of a new type of long-term passive radiation monitor made of lithium.
articles.summary: Glowing salt crystals aboard NASA's Artemis I mission tracked radiation exposure in the Orion spacecraft, providing crucial data for future human lunar exploration.

articles.title: Unveiling Starbirth Mysteries
articles.description: In 1985, the physicist Heinz R. Pagels wrote, "Stars are like animals in the wild. We may see the youung, but never the actual birth, which is a veiled and secret event." In the decades since then, astronomers have drawn closer and closer to figuring out what actually goes in the veiled stellar nurseries throughout the Universe. The tale of starbirth we know today invokes collapse of clouds of gas and dust into prestellar cores, but it still has many unknowns, such as the role of magnetic fields in the clouds where stars are born.
articles.summary: New research unveils mysteries of stellar birth and star formation, helping astronomers better understand how stars are born in the cosmos.
